title: Do not cast API data to any
description: Loads a user object from JSON and casts it to any.
issue_title: Unchecked any cast defeats type safety
issue_description: Casting unknown API data to any removes useful compiler checks and hides contract drift.
issue_suggestion: Parse into unknown and validate or narrow before returning it as User.
issue_code: const data: unknown = await fetch('/api/user').then((r) => r.json());

title: Avoid non-null assertions on optional DOM nodes
description: Clicks an element returned from querySelector.
issue_title: Non-null assertion can hide a runtime null case
issue_description: If the element is missing, the code still crashes at runtime even though the compiler is silenced.
issue_suggestion: Check for null explicitly before using the element.

title: Use discriminated unions for state variants
description: Represents request state with unrelated optional fields.
code: type RequestState = { loading?: boolean; data?: string; error?: string };
issue_title: State shape allows impossible combinations
issue_description: The type permits loading, data, and error to coexist in invalid combinations.
issue_suggestion: Use a discriminated union to model each valid state explicitly.
issue_code: type RequestState = { status: 'loading' } | { status: 'success'; data: string } | { status: 'error'; error: string };

title: Do not ignore promise rejection types
description: Starts an async save without handling rejection.
issue_title: Promise result is dropped without error handling
issue_description: Unhandled rejections become harder to observe and recover from.
issue_suggestion: Await the promise or attach explicit error handling.

title: Prefer readonly for immutable props
description: Accepts a config object that should not be mutated.
code: type Props = { config: { baseUrl: string } };
issue_title: Type does not protect immutable input
issue_description: A mutable config type makes accidental prop mutation easier.
issue_suggestion: Mark immutable object shapes as readonly where appropriate.
issue_code: type Props = { readonly config: { readonly baseUrl: string } };

title: Use exact union values instead of string
description: Models theme mode as any string.
code: type ThemeMode = string;
issue_title: Type is too broad for a fixed domain
issue_description: The compiler cannot catch invalid values like 'bluish' when the real domain is finite.
issue_suggestion: Use a string union for the supported modes.

title: Do not widen empty arrays accidentally
description: Initializes a list without a generic type.
issue_title: Array becomes an unsafe mixed collection
issue_description: Without a declared type, the array can accept unrelated element shapes.
issue_suggestion: Annotate the array with the intended element type.

title: Narrow unknown errors before reading message
description: Reads message from a caught error in strict mode.
issue_title: Caught error is not safely narrowed
issue_description: In TypeScript, catch values are often unknown and must be narrowed before property access.
issue_suggestion: Check the error type before reading message.

title: Prefer interface-compatible callback signatures
description: Accepts a callback with a loosely typed event.
code: type Props = { onChange: (event: any) => void };
issue_title: Callback parameter is typed as any
issue_description: Using any throws away information about the event shape and breaks type checking downstream.
issue_suggestion: Use the specific event type expected by the component.

title: Avoid enum when a literal union is enough
description: Uses an enum for two filter values in a frontend component.
code: enum Filter { Active = 'active', Archived = 'archived' }
issue_title: Enum adds extra runtime output without strong need
issue_description: For simple frontend literals, string unions are often lighter and easier to interoperate with APIs.
issue_suggestion: Use a string union when a runtime enum object is unnecessary.

title: Model optional API fields explicitly
description: Returns a user object that may not have an avatar.
code: type User = { id: string; avatarUrl: string };
issue_title: Type requires a field that the API may omit
issue_description: If the backend omits avatarUrl, callers will trust a value that is not actually present.
issue_suggestion: Mark the field optional or nullable to match the API contract.
issue_code: type User = { id: string; avatarUrl?: string };

title: Preserve generic types through helpers
description: Wraps a fetch helper but returns Promise<any>.
issue_title: Helper erases the response type
issue_description: Returning Promise<any> forces every caller to lose compile-time knowledge about the payload.
issue_suggestion: Make the helper generic over the expected response type.

title: Do not use type assertions for unsafe narrowing
description: Forces a union into one branch using as.
issue_title: Type assertion bypasses the real union guard
issue_description: The code can read data from an error result and fail at runtime.
issue_suggestion: Use the discriminant to narrow the union safely.

title: Prefer Record for keyed maps with known value type
description: Stores feature flags in an object typed as any.
code: const flags: any = { newNavbar: true };
issue_title: Map is untyped
issue_description: Any-typed dictionaries allow inconsistent values and unchecked key usage.
issue_suggestion: Use Record with the intended value type for keyed configuration objects.
issue_code: const flags: Record<string, boolean> = { newNavbar: true };

title: Avoid implicit any in function parameters
description: Leaves a helper parameter untyped.
issue_title: Parameter type is implicit or any
issue_description: Untyped parameters lose editor help and allow invalid call sites.
issue_suggestion: Add a parameter type matching the expected shape.

title: Keep API response nullability in the type
description: Assumes findUser always returns a user.
issue_title: Potential null case is erased
issue_description: If the lookup can return null, the type should force callers to handle that branch.
issue_suggestion: Represent the nullable result and check it before access.
issue_code: const user: User | null = await findUser(userId);

title: Use satisfies to keep literal precision
description: Defines route config with a broad annotation.
code: const routes: Record<string, { method: string }> = { profile: { method: 'GET' } };
issue_title: Literal information is widened away
issue_description: Broad annotation loses useful literal types that can help downstream code.
issue_suggestion: Use satisfies to validate shape while preserving literal precision.
issue_code: const routes = { profile: { method: 'GET' } } satisfies Record<string, { method: string }>;

title: Do not hide unsafe index access
description: Reads from an object map and asserts the entry exists.
code:
const titles: Record<string, string> = {};
const title = titles[id]!;
issue_title: Non-null assertion hides missing-key behavior
issue_description: The map may not contain the requested id even though the compiler warning is suppressed.
issue_suggestion: Handle the missing entry or provide a fallback explicitly.

title: Constrain object keys with keyof
description: Accepts an arbitrary string key to read a user field.
issue_title: Key parameter is too broad
issue_description: Any string is allowed even if it is not a real key on User.
issue_suggestion: Constrain the key parameter with keyof User.
issue_code: function readField(user: User, key: keyof User) {

title: Type async reducers carefully
description: Uses reduce with an async callback but the accumulator type is wrong.
issue_title: Async reducer mixes promise and number types
issue_description: The accumulator becomes a promise after the first iteration and the arithmetic is no longer type-safe.
issue_suggestion: Use an explicit loop or await the accumulator correctly.
issue_code:
let total = 0;
for (const id of ids) total += await fetchValue(id);
